source_text: In contrast, male circumcision's risks—primarily bleeding, infection, and rare penile damage—occur at lower rates (approximately 0.2-0.6% for complications in neonates), while meta-analyses indicate modest benefits like a 50-60% reduction in urinary tract infections in infancy and lowered heterosexual HIV acquisition risk later in life, though these are debated and not universally endorsed as justifying routine practice. [39]
